result.summary: Reviewed git diff main...HEAD directly. The diff touches only test/letflow/definitions/migrations_test.exs (deletes the vacuous refute table_exists_in_schema?("public", table) block + its stale comment, drops ", never in public" from the test name) and test/specs/REQ-027.md (matching correction), exactly per the validated design doc lib/letflow/design/iss-0029-req027-migrations-test-fix.md -- no scope creep, no lib/ or migration changes. Independently re-derived the vacuous-assertion claim from Ecto source rather than trusting ISSUE-FIXER: read deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/migration.ex __prefix__/1 (line 1757) directly -- when a migration table struct has an explicit prefix and the migrator run also supplies one, __prefix__/1 either accepts a match or RAISES on mismatch; it never silently writes to public. Confirmed lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex replay_migrations/2 (line 222) always passes prefix: schema_name (a concrete tenant schema) to Ecto.Migrator.run/4. So under replay_migrations/2 there is no reachable state where a REQ-027 table lands in public -- the refute was structurally unable to fail, confirmed independently rather than taken on the prior diagnosis. Ran empirical checks too (mix/elixir + Postgres available in this sandbox): MIX_ENV=test mix test on both migrations_test.exs files -- 27 tests, 0 failures, positive-half assertion (table lands in tenant schema) intact. Then re-applied ISSUE-FIXER's own mutation (if prefix() do -> if true do in priv/repo/migrations/20260816193001_create_process_definitions.exs line 73) and re-ran test/letflow/event_store/migrations_test.exs: the section-4 guard test (line 484) failed exactly as expected, listing CreateProcessDefinitions among the candidates -- confirming that test genuinely still owns and covers the :prefix-guard property the deleted assertion never could. Reverted the mutation (git checkout --) and confirmed the tree is clean before finishing. Re-ran the full pair of files clean afterward (27/27). No idiomatic-OTP surface applies (test/doc-only change, confirmed explicitly per the handoff task) -- no gen_statem/supervision/type-safety questions are in scope here. One minor, non-blocking nit: 'mix format --check-formatted' flags a stray blank line left at migrations_test.exs:296 (inside the now-shorter for-loop, before 'end') -- a leftover from the deletion that the design doc explicitly instructed to leave untouched (2c). This repo has no CI workflow enforcing mix format, and the blank line has no functional effect, so it does not block this gate; worth a trivial mix format pass next time this file is touched.
